survey: A three-masted sailing ship seen from the port side, bow to the left, sitting low in stylised waves. Hull: a curved wooden hull with plank lines, a scroll-shaped bow, a raised stern deck with a railing, and three brass-rimmed portholes above the waterline. The hull sits in the water, with foam breaking along the waterline. Masts: the fore, main and mizzen masts rise through the deck behind the railing, and each mast's lower part shows below its sail. Each mast has a rope band near the top and ends in a small pennant. All the pennants fly the same way. Yards: one horizontal yard per mast, lashed to the mast with rope bands. Lift lines run from each masthead down to both ends of its yard and form clean triangles. Sails: one square sail per mast, hung from its yard by ring lashings and billowing forward. The main sail hides the main mast between the yard and the sail's foot, which matches a sail hung in front of the mast. Where the sails overlap, the layering is consistent: the main sail is in front of the edges of the fore and mizzen sails. Sheets: ropes run from the sails' lower corners down to the deck and railings, so every rope has two attachment points. No rope ends in the air. Mast count, yard count and sail count agree (3/3/3), and nothing floats or passes through anything else.
